concepts.title: Human Capital and Human Capital Formation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Human Capital and Human Capital Formation' refers to.
questions.a: Human capital formation is the process of adding skills and knowledge to the population through education, health, training, migration and information, making people a productive resource whose returns appear as higher earnings and faster growth.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Human Capital and Human Capital Formation'.
questions.a: Expenditure on education and health is treated as investment in human capital because it raises future productivity, just like investment in physical capital.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Human Capital and Human Capital Formation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Human capital formation (source: keec104.txt human capital sections)

concepts.title: Education Sector in India: Levels, Institutions and Expenditure

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Education Sector in India: Levels, Institutions and Expenditure' refers to.
questions.a: Education in India spans elementary, secondary, higher and adult levels with institutions from primary schools to universities, financed by government and private spending, and literacy rates and enrolment ratios measure progress, with the Right to Education making elementary education a fundamental right.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Education Sector in India: Levels, Institutions and Expenditure'.
questions.a: Government expenditure on education as a percentage of GDP and the rise in literacy rate indicate the growth of the education sector.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Education Sector in India: Levels, Institutions and Expenditure' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Education sector (source: keec104.txt education sector sections)

concepts.title: Unemployment, Human Capital and Economic Growth Linkage

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Unemployment, Human Capital and Economic Growth Linkage' refers to.
questions.a: Human capital formation raises productivity and growth but unemployment wastes human capital; defects of the education system include low public spending, mismatch between education and jobs, brain drain and gender and regional disparities in literacy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unemployment, Human Capital and Economic Growth Linkage'.
questions.a: The chapter stresses that without jobs, educated persons cannot deploy their human capital, weakening the education growth linkage.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Unemployment, Human Capital and Economic Growth Linkage' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Human capital and growth (source: keec104.txt unemployment and growth sections)
